bio: Guests flock here to experience the silence, enjoy the fresh air and, of course, to enjoy locally sourced cuisine which will leave a lasting memory. Although it is located in a village that is a little off the beaten track, it is worth walking from the car park (you have to open and close gates to prevent the animals from escaping) and passing the discreet façade of the house to discover a room where you will see rustic, modern and homely details... and even a typical ‘lareira’ (fireplace), used both for cooking and smoking. Marta and Roberto, the duo at the helm, offer two tasting menus (Viaxe and Travesía), where you will find lovingly prepared traditional dishes, such as scallops and horse mackerel smoked in the lareira or Bandeira oxtail stew....
